analysis.title: FSA Fixed Income Daily Commentary 30 October 2026
key_insights: Treasuries stayed bid: the front end led, with the 2-year yield down 9.9bp to 4.600% and the 10-year down 8bp to 4.939%. The commentary cites the dovish Warsh press conference, a tech sell-off after Alphabet's earnings miss, and lower oil.
The market rejected 4.95% on the 10-year again ahead of the 7-year auction. The auction stopped on the screens and left dealers with 9.4% against a 6-month average of 12.1%.

The ECB held all three policy rates, with the deposit rate at 2.50%. Its statement was dovish on second-round effects but left room for another hike in December. Markets price an 85% chance of a quarter-point hike at year-end and at least one more move in 2027.
US Sept core PCE rose 0.3% m/m, in line with the estimate. Personal income rose 0.2% m/m against an estimate of +0.3%. Q3 GDP rose 3.4% annualized against an estimate of 3.2%.

China Vanke (rated UP) is severely distressed. 9M revenue fell 34.9% y/y to RMB105.0bn and contracted sales fell 48.2%. Net debt is about RMB296bn and about RMB188.69bn of debt is classified as current. Shenzhen Metro provided RMB4.52bn in shareholder loans.

Sinopec Group (MP) is viewed as credit positive. Q3 net profit rose 57.2% under Chinese standards and 9M operating cash flow rose 41.1% to RMB161,994 million, covering capex about twice. Refined product sales fell 11.4% and Chemicals lost money.
AXA (MP) has a Solvency II ratio of 213%, down 5 points in the quarter on market moves. 9M gross written premiums rose 5% to EUR93.0bn and 2026 guidance was kept.
Hyatt (MP) Q3 adjusted EBITDA was USD295m against consensus of USD287.5m. The 2026 RevPAR outlook was raised to 5.0-5.5%, but total debt rose to USD4,430m and liquidity fell to USD1,842m.

Kansai Electric (MP) is viewed as credit negative. H1 operating profit fell 69.9% and recurring profit was well below consensus. Profit attributable held up only through a JPY105bn one-off gain on the sale of shares of an affiliate.

Takeda (MP) is viewed as credit positive. H1 core operating profit of JPY710.6bn beat consensus, FY26 forecasts were raised, and adjusted net debt/EBITDA is 2.5x. Adjusted free cash flow fell to JPY325.7bn from JPY525.4bn.
Gilead (MP) is viewed as credit neutral. Q3 non-GAAP EPS of USD2.55 beat consensus of USD2.12 and HIV sales rose 18%. Cash fell to USD6.4bn from USD10.6bn on USD11.3bn of acquired IPR&D in 9M.
Vale (MP): Q3 adjusted EBITDA fell 24% to USD3.33bn on lower iron ore prices and higher costs, while base metals EBITDA rose 61%. Gross debt including leases was 1.2x LTM EBITDA.

Eurobank (MP): the CET1 ratio is 15.5% with about 120bp of capital to be used for the Eurolife purchase. The NPE ratio is 2.4%, NPE coverage fell to 81.9% from 94.0%, and the 2026 net interest income growth guidance was raised to about 9%.
Starbucks (UP): FY26 adjusted operating income rose 22.2% to USD4.51bn and net debt/EBITDA is 1.9x. Equity is negative at USD7.67bn and dividends took about 76% of free cash flow.
Pitney Bowes (UP): Q3 adjusted EBIT of USD114m beat consensus of USD103.3m. Debt was cut by USD148m in the quarter and 2026 adjusted FCF guidance was raised to USD380-420m.

Intel (MP): Q3 revenue rose 21% to USD16.5bn and data center and AI revenue rose 78%. Net cash is about USD3.9bn after a USD23bn equity offering, and Foundry losses narrowed to USD1.9bn. Q4 guidance implies sequential moderation.
Amazon (MP): Q3 revenue rose 12% to USD201.9bn and AWS rose 39%. TTM free cash flow turned negative at USD42.4bn with capex guidance of about USD220bn. Net debt is about USD58.9bn.

Xerox (UP): leverage is about 8.5x gross and 7.7x net on adjusted operating income. FY26 guidance was cut, dividends were suspended, equity is negative at USD677m, and a USD959m goodwill impairment was booked.

OMV (MP): Q3 clean CCS operating result was EUR2,117m, 2% below consensus. Leverage rose to 17% from 14% after a EUR750m hybrid repayment. 2026 guidance was raised, including Brent above USD95 and a Europe refining margin of about USD25 per barrel.

Repsol (MP): Q3 adjusted net income rose 260% to EUR2.71bn on a refining margin of USD36.2/bbl and Brent at USD97. Net debt fell to EUR2.04bn. 2026 operating cash flow guidance was raised to EUR9.0-9.5bn.

Air Liquide (MP): Q3 revenue rose 10% to EUR7.26bn, above the EUR7.16bn expected. The new BEYOND plan raises shareholder returns, including a EUR4bn buyback through 2028, which the commentary calls a modest deterioration in financial policy for creditors.
Seplat (OP): net debt fell 65% to USD235m, leverage is 0.14x, and the USD100m acquisition facility was repaid. Unit opex guidance was raised and the Yoho restart was delayed.
First Abu Dhabi Bank (MP): 9M net profit rose 3% to AED16.5bn. Net impairments rose 33%, and loans grew 10% YTD against 5% for deposits. The commentary prefers FABUH over EBIUH.
ING (MP): Q3 net profit of EUR1.85bn was about 6% below consensus. Provisions rose to EUR403m and CET1 improved to 13.3%. An additional EUR1.9bn shareholder distribution was announced.

Societe Generale (MP): Q3 net income of EUR1.89bn beat consensus of about EUR1.65bn, and 9M ROTE of 12.3% already exceeds the FY target of about 11%. Moody's outlook is negative while S&P's is positive.

Volkswagen (UP): Q3 operating loss was EUR5.9bn against about EUR2.6bn expected, with EUR8.7bn of exceptional charges. Automotive net liquidity is EUR33bn, and the planned sale of 51% of Everllence to Bain Capital for about EUR7.4bn is pending. S&P and Fitch have negative outlooks.
Akbank (MP): Q3 net income fell 24% q/q and swap-adjusted NIM fell to 2.2% from 3.1%. The NPL ratio rose to 3.7% and management expects Q3 to be the margin trough.

BBVA (MP): Q3 net attributable profit was EUR3.02bn. CET1 fell 69bp q/q to 12.21% and Morningstar DBRS upgraded the bank to AA(low). BBVA Mexico (OP) 9M profit rose 8.4% in constant currency, with an NPL ratio of 2.9%.
Lloyds (OP): Q3 net income rose 9% y/y, CET1 is 13.3%, and FY26 guidance was reaffirmed. The UK bank profit surcharge is temporarily raised to 6%.
RCI Banque (OP) is preferred over Renault. Renault (MP) was upgraded by Moody's to Baa3/Stable on 14 September, restoring investment grade, and Q3 revenue beat consensus.
Banco Sabadell (MP): recurrent Q3 net profit rose 12.9% q/q and CET1 is 13.12%. Headroom above the 13% distribution threshold is limited, and BPCE took a 7% stake.
AB InBev (MP): Q3 normalized EBITDA was USD5.96bn, up 3.9% organically. China volumes fell 16.8%, and net leverage was last reported at 2.86x in June.
Shell (MP): Q3 adjusted earnings of USD10.8bn beat consensus of USD10.3bn. Net debt fell to USD39.7bn despite the ARC Resources acquisition, and the buyback was raised to USD5bn from USD3bn.
Danske Bank (MP): 9M net profit rose 9% to DKK18.3bn, CET1 is 17.2%, and FY26 net profit guidance was narrowed to DKK24-25bn.

Oracle (MP): the Oct 28 Investor Day limited additional capital market funding through FY30 to USD20bn, split equally between debt and equity. 10Y spreads briefly tightened about 40bp before settling near 245bp. The commentary flags about USD220bn of illustrative capex for 6GW of capacity and customer concentration in OpenAI as risks.

Carlsberg (MP): Q3 organic revenue rose 3.0% with volumes up 0.3%. Net debt/EBITDA was 3.28x at FY25 against a target below 2.5x, and the Sapporo JV and the India IPO could help financial flexibility.
Petrobras (MP): Q3 production hit a record 3.51 MMboed. Q3 financials are pending, and 2Q26 net debt was USD60.4bn.
Harley-Davidson (MP): Q3 HDMC revenue fell 10% and 2026 guidance was raised for a second quarter. Shareholder distributions of USD251m YTD exceeded FCF of USD212m.
Bristol Myers (MP): Q3 revenue rose 7% to USD13.07bn, but non-GAAP EPS guidance was cut to USD6.35-6.55 on acquired IPRD charges. Net debt fell to USD29.92bn.

Glencore (OP): H1 adjusted EBITDA rose 86% and net debt is 0.56x EBITDA. The Radiant World/Sapphire Minmetals dispute involves claims of about USD2bn, and Glencore puts its net exposure below USD500m.
Mashreq (MP): loans grew 33% y/y, the loan/deposit ratio rose to 80% from 74%, and CET1 and LCR declined q/q.
TotalEnergies (MP): Q3 adjusted EBITDA was USD17.81bn and gearing fell to 9.1% from 13.1%. Much of the profit comes from exceptional refining margins that may normalize.
Caterpillar (MP): Q3 sales rose 17% to USD20.7bn with a record USD72bn backlog. Merck (MP): Q3 sales rose 5% to USD18.09bn, GAAP gross margin fell to 72.9% and net interest expense rose.
Mastercard (MP): Q3 net revenue rose 14% to USD9.81bn with an adjusted operating margin of 60.5%. Altria (MP): Q3 net income was USD2.52bn, with capital returns tilted heavily toward shareholders.
YPF (MP): LTM net leverage fell to a record-low 0.8x, free cash flow was USD888m, and a USD1.2bn international bond was issued in September.

market_movers.rationale: Severely distressed credit with 9M revenue down 34.9% and contracted sales down 48.2%. About RMB188.69bn of debt is current against RMB52.45bn of cash.
Sinopec Group, MP. Credit positive: operating cash flow rose 41.1% and covered capex about twice.
AXA, MP. The Solvency II ratio of 213% is a wide cushion but fell 5 points in the quarter.
Hyatt, MP. Credit neutral: Q3 EBITDA beat consensus, but debt rose and liquidity fell.
Kansai Electric, MP. Credit negative: H1 operating profit fell 69.9%, and profit held up only on a one-off gain.
Takeda, MP. Credit positive: core operating profit beat consensus and FY26 forecasts were raised.
Gilead, MP. Credit neutral: the HIV franchise funds the business, but cash fell on acquired IPR&D.
Vale, MP. Leverage is 1.2x, but iron ore profitability is falling.
Eurobank, MP. Credit positive: CET1 is 15.5%, but NPE coverage fell.
Starbucks, UP. Leverage is improving, but negative equity and shareholder distributions constrain flexibility.
Pitney Bowes, UP. Deleveraging continues, but SendTech revenue is in structural decline.
Intel, MP. Net cash was funded by a USD23bn equity raise, and Foundry losses continue.
Amazon, MP on fair valuations. Free cash flow is negative at USD42.4bn on AI capex.
Xerox, UP. Leverage is about 8.5x, guidance was cut, dividends were suspended, and equity is negative.
OMV, MP. The leverage ratio rose to 17% after the hybrid repayment, and credit depends on Fuels and Energy margins.
Repsol, MP. Net leverage is about 0.1x, helped by unusually favorable commodity conditions.
Air Liquide, MP. The capital allocation policy is more shareholder-friendly and leverage is higher after the Airgas acquisition.
Seplat, OP. Net debt is down 65% and leverage is 0.14x, offset by Nigeria sovereign risk.
First Abu Dhabi Bank, MP. Impairments are rising and loans are growing faster than deposits. The commentary prefers FABUH over EBIUH.
ING, MP. Q3 profit missed consensus and provisions rose, while capital is strong.
Societe Generale, MP. Q3 results beat, but FICC revenue was weak and distributions are large.
Volkswagen, UP. Operating performance is credit negative, with Q3 operating loss of EUR5.9bn. Automotive net liquidity of EUR33bn cushions bondholders.
Akbank, MP. Profitability is under pressure and asset quality is slowly deteriorating.
BBVA, MP. Strong earnings, but CET1 fell 69bp q/q.
BBVA Mexico, OP. Dominant franchise and a 30.7% efficiency ratio, offset by rising retail delinquencies.
Lloyds, OP. Strong capital generation and FY26 guidance reaffirmed, offset by motor finance redress risk.
RCI Banque, OP. Preferred over Renault debt on double-digit revenue growth and diversified funding.
Renault, MP. Q3 beat expectations, but Dacia weakness and reliance on 2H cash generation remain. The commentary prefers exposure through Mobilize Financial Services.
Banco Sabadell, MP. Improving profitability, but limited headroom above the 13% distribution threshold.
AB InBev, MP. China weakness and rising distributions limit credit upside. The commentary favors intermediate maturities.
Shell, MP. Strong cash flow and deleveraging, with exposure to commodity price normalization.
Danske Bank, MP. Strong profitability and capital, but higher distributions and weaker trading income limit upside.
Oracle, MP. The financing roadmap is credit positive, but the scale of investment and leverage warrant caution.
Carlsberg, MP. Leverage is elevated and beer volumes are weak.
Petrobras, MP. Record production, but Q3 financials are pending and the commentary awaits confirmation of deleveraging.
Harley-Davidson, MP. Moderately credit positive, but industrial profitability is weak and distributions exceeded FCF.
Bristol Myers Squibb, MP. Net debt is falling, but margins are under pressure and the Eliquis patent cliff approaches.
Glencore, OP. Low leverage and strong cash generation, with the Radiant World dispute as an event risk.
Mashreq, MP. Rapid lending growth is reducing capital and liquidity ratios.
TotalEnergies, MP. Gearing fell to 9.1%, but profit depends on exceptional refining margins.
Caterpillar, MP. Record backlog of USD72bn, with buybacks as a cash drain.
Merck, MP. Strong sales, but gross margin and leverage are deteriorating.
Mastercard, MP. Asset-light model with a 60.5% operating margin, and buybacks outpace equity growth.
Altria, MP. Stable free cash flow, but heavy equity-biased capital allocation and cigarette volume decline.
YPF, MP. Leverage is at a record-low 0.8x, but the company depends on Argentine regulation and Vaca Muerta growth.

sector_views.rationale: Q3 results at Shell, Repsol, TotalEnergies and OMV were strong on record refining margins and Brent near USD97. The commentary warns the margins may be unsustainable. All four issuers are MP.
Most are MP with strong capital. Rising shareholder distributions limit capital accumulation, and provisions are rising at several names. Lloyds and BBVA Mexico are OP.
Volkswagen is UP with a Q3 operating loss of EUR5.9bn. Renault is MP, and RCI Banque is preferred over Renault.
Takeda, Gilead, BMS and Merck are all MP. Patent expirations and acquired IPR&D charges weigh on EPS.
Vanke remains severely distressed, with contracted sales down 48%.

earnings_insights: Gilead Q3: non-GAAP EPS USD2.55 reported against consensus USD2.12, GAAP EPS USD1.94.
Hyatt Q3: adjusted EBITDA USD295m reported against consensus USD287.5m, adjusted diluted EPS USD1.27.
Pitney Bowes Q3: adjusted EPS USD0.42 reported against consensus USD0.34, adjusted EBIT USD114m reported against consensus USD103.3m.
Takeda H1: core operating profit JPY710.6bn reported against company-compiled consensus JPY671.2bn. Revenue JPY2,407.0bn reported against consensus JPY2,373.8bn.
Intel Q3: revenue USD16.5bn reported, GAAP EPS USD0.60, non-GAAP EPS USD0.52. Q4 guide is revenue USD15.0-16.0bn and GAAP EPS USD0.10.
Amazon Q3: revenue USD201.9bn reported, operating income USD28.1bn, diluted EPS USD1.89. Q4 guide is revenue USD240-247bn and operating income USD28.5-33.5bn.
Xerox Q3: adjusted EPS USD0.02 reported, adjusted operating income USD124m. FY26 adjusted operating income guide was cut to USD450-475mn from USD555-605mn.
OMV Q3: clean CCS operating result EUR2,117m reported against company-collected consensus EUR2,168m. Clean CCS EPS EUR3.54.
Repsol Q3: adjusted net income EUR2.71bn reported against EUR752m in Q3 2025.
Eurobank Q3: adjusted net profit EUR433m reported against company-compiled consensus EUR417m.
ING Q3: net profit EUR1.85bn reported against consensus EUR1.97bn.
Societe Generale Q3: net income EUR1.89bn reported against consensus of about EUR1.65bn.
Shell Q3: adjusted earnings USD10.8bn reported against consensus USD10.3bn.
Kansai Electric H1: recurring profit JPY111,550m reported against consensus JPY165.7bn.
Volkswagen Q3: operating loss EUR5.9bn reported against about EUR2.6bn expected.
BBVA Q3: net attributable profit EUR3.02bn reported, broadly in line with consensus. Impairments of EUR1.95bn were above consensus.
Merck Q3: worldwide sales USD18.09bn reported, GAAP gross margin 72.9%. FY26 revenue outlook is USD66.8-67.3bn.
Bristol Myers Q3: non-GAAP EPS USD1.35 reported, including a USD0.58 hit from acquired IPRD. Non-GAAP EPS guide was cut to USD6.35-6.55.
Starbucks Q4 FY26: adjusted EPS USD0.80 reported. FY27 guide is adjusted EPS of USD3.15-3.25.
Air Liquide Q3: revenue EUR7.26bn reported against market expectations of EUR7.16bn.

macro_indicators.interpretation: In line with the 0.3% estimate and not accelerating, which was enough to drive a Treasury rally and short covering.
Consensus estimate for the Sept print.
All three rates held. Markets price an 85% chance of another quarter-point hike at year-end.
Slightly below the median forecast of 35.1.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer First Abu Dhabi Bank (FABUH) over EBIUH at current valuations
trade_ideas.rationale: The commentary maintains MP on FAB and continues to prefer FABUH over EBIUH.
trade_ideas.risk: Regulatory flexibility on borrower staging could obscure emerging stress.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer RCI Banque over Renault automotive debt
trade_ideas.rationale: The captive's recurring financing income and funding franchise support an attractive credit profile.
trade_ideas.risk: Rising credit costs, auto sector weakness and parent concentration.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer exposure to Renault through Mobilize Financial Services
trade_ideas.rationale: Recurring financing income and an established funding franchise.
Results were in line, so limited spread implications.
Exceptionally low leverage and improving credit quality.
trade_ideas.risk: Oil-price sensitivity, infrastructure reliability, Nigeria sovereign risk.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Glencore bonds across the curve
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong cash generation, low leverage and substantial liquidity.
trade_ideas.risk: Radiant World dispute, commodity price sensitivity, shareholder distributions.

risk_factors: Distressed Chinese property: Vanke has about RMB188.69bn of current debt against RMB52.45bn of cash.
Commodity price normalization could reverse record refining margins at Shell, Repsol, TotalEnergies and OMV.
Rising shareholder distributions are limiting capital build at European banks and several corporates.
AI capex funding: Amazon's free cash flow is negative USD42.4bn and Oracle plans about USD220bn of illustrative capex with OpenAI concentration.
Chinese consumer weakness is hitting AB InBev, Carlsberg and Volkswagen volumes.
Auto sector pressure, including Volkswagen's operating loss and negative outlooks from S&P and Fitch.
Rising provisions and asset-quality drift at Akbank, ING, BBVA Mexico, FAB and Mashreq.
Middle East disruption to energy production and supply.
vol_and_positioning: The Treasury market rejected 4.95% on the 10-year again before the 7-year auction.
The 5s/30s curve steepened 3bp as the front end led the rally.
Oracle 10Y credit spreads tightened about 40bp after the Investor Day and settled near 245bp. 30Y spreads were near 285bp.
geopolitical: Middle East disruption continues to affect Shell's Qatar production, where repairs to the Pearl gas-to-liquids facility are ongoing.
TotalEnergies attributes elevated commodity prices to ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.
First Abu Dhabi Bank carries a conflict-related ECL overlay of AED350m, and the CBUAE extended temporary relief until January 2027.
The DRC cobalt export restrictions affecting Glencore remain in place until at least end-2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Shell, Repsol, TotalEnergies and OMV reported record Q3 refining margins, for example Repsol at USD36.2/bbl, with sharply lower net debt.
tension_points.bear_case: The commentary says the margins may be unsustainable and could normalize, and that earnings are exposed to commodity price normalization.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A fall in the refining indicator margin from the around USD25 per barrel OMV now guides.

tension_points.bull_case: Oracle's financing roadmap limits new capital market funding to USD20bn through FY30 and targets positive free cash flow in 2H FY28. Intel's net cash position came from a USD23bn equity raise.
tension_points.bear_case: Amazon's free cash flow is negative USD42.4bn. Oracle plans about USD220bn of illustrative capex and relies on vendor financing, which is economically debt-like.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Delays at Oracle's New Mexico and Wisconsin data centres, or loss of the OpenAI customer.

tension_points.bull_case: Dovish Warsh press conference, lower oil, a Tech sell-off after Alphabet's earnings miss and in-line core PCE drove short covering.
tension_points.bear_case: The 10-year has rejected 4.95% twice, and the 7-year auction had a below-average dealer takedown.
